narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and based on an automated assessment of your financial profile, the system determined there is an 85% likelihood that you represent a high credit risk — a threshold that unfortunately led to the denial of your application. This does not reflect a judgment about you as a person, but rather a pattern the system identified in your specific financial circumstances at this time.

The single most influential factor in this decision was the size of the loan you requested. At 15,672 DM, your requested amount is dramatically higher than what typical approved applicants seek — the average among those who were approved is around 2,887 DM. This means you are requesting more than five times the typical approved loan amount, which the system interpreted as a strong signal of elevated financial risk, particularly given the context of 1970s Germany where average annual salaries ranged between 10,000 and 20,000 DM.

Closely tied to this concern is the duration of your requested loan. You applied for a 48-month repayment period, while approved applicants repay their loans in roughly 19 months on average. A longer repayment window increases the uncertainty around whether obligations will be met over time, and combined with the large loan amount, this paints a picture of a very substantial, long-term financial commitment that the system flagged as risky.

The third important factor was the status of your checking account, which currently holds between 0 and 200 DM. While this is not the worst possible situation — some approved applicants also fall into this category — having a low checking account balance alongside a very large loan request and a long repayment term compounded the concern. A healthier account balance would have provided some reassurance that you have a financial cushion to manage repayments.

On a more positive note, your credit history shows existing credits being paid on time, which is actually the most common profile among approved applicants, and your employment of 1 to 4 years is also well within the range seen among those who were approved. These factors work in your favor and suggest you are not without financial responsibility.

To improve your chances in the future, you might consider applying for a significantly smaller loan amount, as this alone would bring your profile much closer to that of approved applicants. You could also explore whether a shorter repayment period is feasible, or whether building up your checking account savings before reapplying would strengthen your application. Speaking directly with a bank advisor could help you identify a loan structure that better fits what lenders are comfortable approving given your current financial standing.
